column2: House-building mechanics – gather resources, construct structures, upgrade, demolish, rebuild.
Survival cycle – collect food, cook it, eat, track hunger/thirst levels across a full day-night cycle.
Combat mechanics – fight animals and mystical creatures (attack, defense, dodge, retreat).
Exploration – traverse forest (dense jungle, rivers, cliffs, caves), observe transitions between areas.
Weather & environment – test effects of rain, fog, storms, and night lighting on visibility and gameplay.
Inventory management – collect, stack, drop, trade, and use items (check limits & sorting).
Save/load system – save during different states (combat, building, exploration) and reload to verify persistence.
Resource gathering – chop trees, mine rocks, hunt animals, pick plants → verify yield and respawn cycles.
Death & respawn loop – die from combat, starvation, or environment, then respawn and continue.
User interface & controls – check menus, tooltips, responsiveness across input devices.
Check for collision bugs – walk through walls/trees, attack through obstacles, fall through terrain.
Physics issues – drop items on cliffs/water → do they vanish, duplicate, or behave oddly?
Inventory exploits – overfill backpack, duplicate items by quick-drop or save/load.
Combat edge cases – kill creature exactly as you die, or log out mid-battle.
Performance/memory – long play sessions (4+ hours), many structures → look for slowdown or crashes.
Graphical glitches – textures missing at night, animations frozen, clipping of models.
